channel.title: Humanoid Robots News
channel.description: Daily high-signal humanoid robot news: launches, deployments, funding, notable demos and robot foundation models. One item per story.

item.title: Boston Dynamics reportedly lines up an all-Korean Atlas supply chain and tells suppliers to prepare parts for 10,000 humanoids
item.description:
Boston Dynamics has finalized its supplier lineup for the Atlas humanoid and asked the selected companies to get ready for purchase orders covering 10,000 units, KED Global reported on Oct 27, citing industry sources. This is a report, not confirmed by Boston Dynamics, and it describes a request to prepare, not a placed order.

  • Actuators and grippers: Hyundai Mobis, with actuators said to make up most of the robot's parts cost.
  • Batteries: Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution; cameras from a Mobis-led group with Namuga and IL, plus MCNEX and Cammsys for hand cameras.
  • Other parts: BH EVS for charging and CTR for control arms; the only non-Korean component is NVIDIA's processor.

Final quantities and prices aren't set, and first orders are expected around late 2027 or early 2028. Early Atlas units are slated for Hyundai's own Metaplant in Georgia. Machine Economy's breakdown stresses that the 10,000 figure is a planning number, not a shipment or contract.

item.title: Unitree's first earnings since its IPO: Q3 revenue up 70% to 665M yuan, but net profit falls 17% as R&D spending jumps
item.description:
Unitree Robotics reported its first quarterly results since its August listing in Shanghai, per the South China Morning Post and the company's Q3 filing.

  • Q3 revenue rose 69.93% year on year to 665 million yuan (about $100 million).
  • Net profit fell 17.37% to 112.7 million yuan, well below the roughly 224 million yuan analysts expected, according to Reuters.
  • Quarterly R&D spending jumped about 250% to 127 million yuan, around 19% of revenue, as Unitree invests in robot AI.
  • For the first nine months, revenue grew 55.7% to 1.82 billion yuan.

It's an early market test for China's best-known humanoid maker amid a tech-sector selloff.

item.title: XPeng's dedicated solid-state battery for the IRON humanoid enters small-batch production ahead of robot mass production
item.description:
XPeng vice president Gu Jie said at the Society of Automotive Engineers of China annual conference on Oct 28 that solid-state batteries built for the IRON humanoid have started rolling off the line in small batches, CnEVPost reports. IRON itself is still before start of production, with mass production planned by the end of 2026 and commercial deployment in stores from 2027.

  • The pack uses a high-energy-density design for the robot's tight internal space and is built to stop thermal runaway from spreading; it passes impact and nail-penetration tests.
  • Gu reportedly said it's about 30% lighter with about 30% more capacity than the previous pack (per a post on X).
  • Unclear: XPeng didn't say whether this is the all-solid-state chemistry it promised in 2025; a September report said the production IRON would use semi-solid-state cells instead. No volume or energy-density figures were given.

item.title: Westlake Robotics shows an upgraded WR1 model running humanoids through multi-room household chores without resets
item.description:
Hangzhou start-up Westlake Robotics, spun out of Westlake University, released videos of an improved version of its WR1 AI model, Vuntum reports.

  • A humanoid takes trousers and a T-shirt off a rack, then folds the trousers together with a second humanoid.
  • In a second run across kitchen, living room and bedroom, it moves corn from the fridge to an air-fryer basket, kneels to pick up toys, and straightens a duvet.

The company says the tasks run in sequence with no human resets or step-by-step prompting. These are company-made demo videos, and the cooking stops at the fryer basket.

item.title: Reward AI shows its glove-trained OM-1 model driving humanoids on last-mile delivery and stairs
item.description:
Robotics startup Reward AI, whose team previously built DexCap, HumanPlus and ALOHA, posted new videos of its OM-1 robot model running humanoids indoors and outdoors: unloading Amazon, Walmart and DHL packages from a Cybertruck bed for last-mile delivery, and picking things up while standing on stairs.

OM-1 is trained only on data from people wearing Reward AI's 7-degree-of-freedom Omnibody Hand glove, with no teleoperation and no on-robot data, and the company says one policy runs across arms and humanoids. The post drew about 430 likes and 64,000 views within hours.

  • These are company-run stress tests, not a commercial rollout.
  • No weights, code or API have been released.

Sources: Reward AI on X, Reward AI OM-1 blog post.

item.title: Shanghai's International Embodied Intelligence Competition puts about 1,000 humanoid robots through real-world tasks
item.description:
The International Embodied Intelligence Competition wrapped up in Shanghai on Sunday, with about 1,000 humanoid robots from more than 800 teams competing across 23 categories spanning industrial production, services, special operations and everyday life.

The event was the centerpiece of the 2026 Global Developer Pioneers Summit, which drew more than 300 robot hardware companies and over 200 supply-chain firms. A Pudong official said more than 30 humanoid models have launched in the district, calling it the world's densest cluster of mass-produced humanoids (an official claim, not independently verified).

Source: China Daily.

item.title: AgiBot launches Genie G2 Max, a heavy-payload wheeled humanoid lifting up to 50 kg, already in JD Logistics warehouses
item.description:
AgiBot released the Genie G2 Max, a safety-rated dual-arm embodied robot for depalletizing, palletizing, material transfer and production-line feeding. It is the third launch in AgiBot's "AI WAVE" release week.

  • Payload of 20 kg per arm, 40 kg rated with both arms and 50 kg peak, with arm repeatability within 0.5 mm.
  • A waist pitch joint lets it lean forward, so pallets can sit against a wall without a walkway behind them.
  • Hot-swappable dual batteries and self-charging for round-the-clock work.

AgiBot says the robot already depalletizes 80 cases and palletizes 75 cases an hour at a JD Logistics warehouse with over 99% success, and feeds parts on its own humanoid production line. Those figures are the company's own, and no price was given. The robot will be shown at AgiBot Innovation Day on Oct 29.

Source: Robrief.

item.title: Humanoid maker CASBOT closes A++ round worth several hundred million yuan, citing over RMB 400M in shoemaking-robot orders
item.description:
Beijing-based CASBOT, maker of the full-size CASBOT 02 humanoid, the wheeled-arm W2 and the half-size Mini, completed an A++ round worth "several hundred million yuan," according to China Securities Journal and Science and Technology Daily. The exact amount was not disclosed.

The company says it holds more than RMB 400 million (about $56M) in 2026 orders for shoemaking robots, with production planned in the thousands of units. At a footwear factory in Putian, its lightweight perception-to-action model runs arms that stamp an outsole every 7 seconds. Its claimed 50% to 70% annual ROI for customers has not been independently verified.

The money goes to mass-production delivery, model development and market expansion.

Source: Humanoid Beat.

item.title: Agility expands Digit to two more GXO warehouses and adds three unnamed manufacturing customers
item.description:
Agility Robotics says GXO, the first company to put its Digit humanoid into live commercial work, will deploy Digit at two more U.S. facilities in Statesville, North Carolina, and Lebanon, Tennessee, starting in early 2027. Those sites start on Digit 4 and move to Digit 5 once it ships. Digit has moved more than 100,000 totes at GXO's Flowery Branch, Georgia site since June 2024.

In the same update, Agility described three new paid manufacturing customers that asked not to be named:

  • A global automaker that sells more than three million vehicles a year
  • One of the world's largest automotive technology and components developers
  • A leading global consumer products manufacturer

Agility also says it has more than 30 prospective customers in its pipeline, including two early-stage potential subcontractor deals for a branch of the U.S. Armed Services (no agreements signed). It repeated its previously disclosed figure of more than $300 million in multi-year Digit 5 orders and expects its SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI to close in Q4 2026, trading on Nasdaq as AGLT.

Sources: Agility press release, GXO and Agility announcement, Agility on X

item.title: China publishes its first six national humanoid robot standards, effective April 2027
item.description:
China's State Administration for Market Regulation has released the country's first six national standards for humanoid robots. They take effect on April 1, 2027.

  • Five documents form the GB/T 48317 series: general technical requirements, environmental perception, decision-making and planning, movement control, and task execution.
  • A sixth, GB/T 48316-2026, sets specifications for humanoid simulation testing platforms.

The standards are voluntary (GB/T) rather than mandatory, but they give buyers and makers a common way to measure and compare humanoid capabilities across very different hardware and control stacks. Major Chinese robot makers took part in drafting them.

Source: Robot24

item.title: Realbotix opens reservations for Echo companion humanoids at $11,950 tabletop and $59,950 full-body
item.description:
Realbotix (TSXV: XBOT) launched Echo, a line of conversational humanoid robots aimed at companionship, education and wellness, and opened $199 reservations.

  • Tabletop Echo: $11,950, 17 degrees of freedom, 225 units planned for 2027.
  • Full-body Echo: $59,950, 39 degrees of freedom with articulated fingers, 25 units planned for 2027.
  • A required AI subscription starts at $19.99 a month; an optional on-device Vinci vision add-on costs $24,950.
  • Four personas (Aria, Mila, Dave, Amar); U.S.-only deliveries expected in the second half of 2027.

Some people on X questioned whether the promo video and images were AI-generated; Realbotix says it will show Echo in person at CES 2027.

Sources: Robotics 24/7, Realbotix pricing page

item.title: Unitree's new H2-X security humanoid loses a leg after a failed side flip at a public demo
item.description:
Unitree's H2-X humanoid, launched on October 21 as the "Kung Fu Legend: Guardian" for security patrols and emergency rescue, fell while landing a side flip at the World Physical AI Conference in Hangzhou. One lower leg detached completely at the joint, and attendee footage spread quickly across social media.

Unitree had promoted the H2-X with videos of it denting car doors, lifting the front of a vehicle and backflipping off a four-meter platform, and claims about eight hours of battery life. As of TechNode's report, Unitree had not publicly explained the failure.

Source: TechNode

item.title: AgiBot runs 110 production Expedition A3 humanoids in sync for a Guinness World Record
item.description:
Chinese humanoid maker AgiBot coordinated 110 full-size Expedition A3 humanoids in a synchronized dance in Jinan on October 24, and a Guinness World Records judge certified it as the most humanoid robots dancing at once. The routine ran about 5 minutes 43 seconds with jumps, flips and formation changes.

  • The robots are standard production units, coordinated by AgiBot's LinkBots cluster-control platform with ultra-wideband positioning for centimeter-level accuracy.
  • AgiBot says the fleet will next go into cultural and tourism shows, public services, research and education. Posts on X say units are already on trial in subway stations; that part is unconfirmed.
  • The demo lands as China's industry ministry says Chinese firms built more than 40,000 humanoids in the first half of 2026, though Global Times notes most real-world uses are still pilots.

Sources: Humanoids Daily, Global Times, Pandaily on X.

item.title: ETH Zürich teaches a Unitree G1 humanoid to climb, vault and get up from falls with one contact-planning policy
item.description:
Researchers at ETH Zürich's Robotic Systems Lab, with Apple, the ETH AI Center and NVIDIA, showed a Unitree G1 climbing ladders, scaling obstacles, crossing sparse footholds and recovering from falls using a single learned policy called Attention-based Contact Planning (ACP).

  • Instead of scripting each move, ACP decides where the robot's hands, feet and body should touch the environment, and the controller works out the motion between those contacts.
  • It was trained on just 13.2 minutes of human motion data plus reinforcement learning, and runs without reference motions once deployed.
  • The team reports 92.5% average success on eight simulated obstacle courses versus 58.8% for its baseline. That is a simulation number, not a measured real-world rate, and the paper (submitted to arXiv October 22) is still under review.

Sources: Humanoids Daily, RoboHub demo clip on X.

item.title: Alibaba's Amap open-sources λ0, a whole-body humanoid model trained mostly on first-person human video
item.description:
Amap, Alibaba's mapping business, and Alibaba's Token Hub team have released λ0 (lambda zero), a model that controls a humanoid robot's whole body for walking plus manipulation. Most of what it learns comes from about 500 hours of first-person video of people doing everyday tasks rather than from robot data.

  • On the team's own real-world tests with a Unitree G1, λ0 finished 62.5% of trials versus 40% for π0.5, the strongest rival model they tested. These are the team's own numbers and haven't been reproduced independently.
  • The code is open under Apache 2.0, and a mid-training checkpoint built on Qwen3.5-2B is on Hugging Face. The training datasets and the full deployment workflow are not released yet, and the model card says it is not a deployment-ready robot policy.

Sources: TSN, arXiv preprint, GitHub repo, Hugging Face checkpoint.

item.title: Tesla says its first production Optimus robots will go to an "Optimus Academy" of 10,000 to 20,000 bots learning by self-play
item.description:
The first Optimus robots coming off Tesla's new Fremont line won't go to customers. Tesla says they will be used in an "Optimus Academy" to collect training data, and Elon Musk said on the Q3 earnings call that Tesla needs on the order of 10,000 to 20,000 robots practicing a wide range of tasks through self-play to make Optimus useful in the real world. The plan became one of X's top robotics stories today.

  • Musk compared it to raising a toddler: robots start wobbly and learn by playing at scale, since Optimus has no equivalent of Tesla's car fleet generating data.
  • Tesla AI lead Ashok Elluswamy said the robots will first learn by watching humans, then bootstrap with self-play.
  • Musk said the hands still aren't perfected, reaching 20,000 robots a week will take at least a year, the AI5 chip should reach the robot around April 2027, and deliveries to other companies are targeted for late 2027. These are company targets, not confirmed timelines.

Sources: The Next Web, Fierce Sensors, X trending story.

item.title: Generative Bionics plans Europe's largest physical AI data factory for its Gene.01 humanoids, with AMD
item.description:
Italian humanoid maker Generative Bionics says it will build what it calls Europe's largest physical AI training facility, using AMD computing to pair real robot work with large-scale digital twin simulation.

  • The first 5,000-square-meter site will be in Italy and is scheduled to open by Q4 2027, the first of a planned three-site network.
  • Fleets of its Gene.01 humanoids will run tasks continuously in recreated industrial settings to generate data for training World Action Models, with simulated variations fed back to the physical robots in a real-to-sim-to-real loop.
  • AMD Ventures took part in the company's €70 million seed round, and AMD chips already run on board Gene.01.

Source: Robotics & Automation News.

item.title: South Korea names Mobilint to lead humanoid-robot chip work in its $606M on-device AI semiconductor program
item.description:
Seoul NPU startup Mobilint was named lead research organization for the humanoid robotics arm of South Korea's ₩800.2 billion (about $606 million) K-On-Device AI Semiconductor program, which runs from 2026 to 2030.

  • Mobilint is responsible for a co-designed NPU and software stack for running AI on the robot itself, covering the chip, compiler and a module that can be installed in robot bodies.
  • The platform will be tested in stages inside LG Electronics' home robot platform.
  • Mobilint raised a ₩70 billion (about $53 million) Series C in April 2026.

Source: Tech Times.

item.title: NEURA Robotics unveils 4NE1 Gen 4 humanoid for serial production and opens TUM RoboGym near Munich
item.description:
German robot maker NEURA Robotics has unveiled 4NE1 Gen 4, a humanoid it says is designed for serial production and is 20 percent lighter than the previous generation.

  • The new robot has a slimmer build with a black textile outer skin, hands with touch and force sensing, and independently reacting "Smart Limbs" for faster, smoother motion.
  • It runs Neuron AI, NEURA's own foundation model for physical AI, and is already learning real-world tasks daily at the company's NEURA Gyms.
  • The launch coincides with the opening of the TUM RoboGym, a 2,300-square-meter training center near Munich Airport built with the Technical University of Munich. The three-year partnership is worth about €17 million, with NEURA contributing about €11 million.
  • NEURA plans more training centers in Europe, the US and China, plus another German site with RWTH Aachen. No price or shipping date was given.

Source: Interesting Engineering.

item.title: LG hires Hyundai's former Robotics Lab chief Hyun Dong-jin to lead group physical AI and humanoid push (report)
item.description:
LG Group has hired Hyun Dong-jin, who ran Hyundai Motor Group's Robotics Lab for about seven years, as executive vice president for physical AI at LG Science Park, according to an exclusive report from the Korea Economic Daily on Oct 23.

  • Hyun reportedly started this month and will act as the control tower for LG's long-term robot business, tying together robotics work spread across LG affiliates, including next-generation humanoid development.
  • At Hyundai he led the MobED mobile robot platform and the X-ble Shoulder wearable robot before leaving in April.
  • LG plans to unveil a bipedal humanoid in the first quarter of 2027. The hire lands amid a talent war among Korea's biggest groups: Samsung hired a former Boston Dynamics-linked robotics executive in July, and Hyundai recruited a former Samsung robotics leader.

Unconfirmed: neither LG nor Hyundai has officially announced the appointment.

Sources: KED Global, MEKAWIRE.

item.title: Figure 03 keeps walking: 13 straight days, 422 miles and 1.5 million steps on a treadmill stress test
item.description:
Figure CEO Brett Adcock posted on Oct 23 that a Figure 03 humanoid has now walked nonstop on a treadmill for 13 days, covering 422 miles and 1.5 million steps.

  • The run started as a side project to stress the robot and surface any hardware failures. Adcock first shared it on Oct 19 at 9 days and 348 miles, in a post seen by more than 500,000 people.
  • It's an informal endurance test rather than a commercial deployment, but it's an unusually long public durability demo for a humanoid's legs and actuators.
  • Separately, Figure researcher Corey Lynch said the company now processes about 81 minutes of video per second for robot pretraining, which Adcock described as building "a startup inside of a startup."

Sources: Brett Adcock's update on X, his original Oct 19 post, Corey Lynch on Figure's video data scale.

item.title: XPENG's IRON humanoid switches between handshakes, fist bumps and high-fives in real time with VLA 2.0
item.description:
XPENG released an R&D test video of its IRON humanoid reading a person's hand gestures and changing its response mid-motion, with no voice commands.

  • As the person switches between offering a handshake, a fist bump and a high-five, IRON adapts, including switching hands for a high-five.
  • XPENG says IRON's VLA 2.0 model re-evaluates what it sees every 0.2 seconds and predicts motion over the next six seconds.
  • This is a company-produced demo of social interaction, not a deployment, and XPENG hasn't shared independent test results.

Sources: Humanoids Daily, Cocoloop.

item.title: Figure 04 humanoid hits full design lock as Figure shares its internal all-hands publicly
item.description:
Figure CEO Brett Adcock published the company's internal all-hands meeting on X on Oct 22, saying Figure's roadmap "has completely changed over the last year" and the team has doubled.

  • The headline milestone: Figure 04, the company's fourth-generation humanoid, has reached full design lock, and Figure has started shipping parts for it.
  • Adcock calls it Figure's biggest hardware leap yet, an "iPhone 1 moment," aimed at easier manufacturing at the BotQ plant, lower cost, and home safety.
  • No specs, price, or launch date were given, and the robot was shown blurred. Figure 03 stays the commercial product for now.

Sources: Humanoids Daily, Humanoid Guide, Brett Adcock's post on X.

item.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon teaches Apptronik's Apollo humanoid a skill straight from video
item.description:
As part of the Gemini 4 Argon launch, Google DeepMind showed a "Video-to-Sim-to-Real" pipeline: Argon watched raw video of a person playing cornhole, mapped the scene, worked out the whole-body joint motions, and wrote its own simulation code. The learned behavior was then transferred to Apptronik's Apollo humanoid.

  • DeepMind says Apollo landed seven consecutive shots in a real-world trial.
  • It says the pipeline compresses weeks of manual simulation modeling into a few hours.
  • Argon scored 87% on DeepMind's Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark. These results are DeepMind's own internal tests.

Source: Robotics & Automation News.

item.title: Agility standardizes Digit 5 on NVIDIA IGX Thor; reports over $300M in Digit 5 orders
item.description:
Agility Robotics said on Oct 22 that the general-availability version of Digit 5 will use NVIDIA IGX Thor modules as its only onboard computer, making NVIDIA the exclusive compute supplier. Agility is also folding more NVIDIA Halos safety models into Digit's human-detection system, and NVIDIA's Halos inspection lab will review Digit's safety software ahead of third-party certification.

  • Early access to Digit 5 is expected in the first half of 2027, with wider availability over the following six to nine months.
  • Agility says it has more than $300 million in multi-year Digit 5 orders (subject to contract milestones), four new customers, and a new 50,000 sq ft Pittsburgh site.
  • It's the company's fourth announcement in four days as it heads toward a Nasdaq listing (ticker AGLT) via its Churchill Capital XI merger.

Sources: Agility press release, The Next Web.

item.title: Unitree unveils "Unitree Rehearsal," a self-improving AI loop for humanoid development
item.description:
Unitree founder Wang Xingxing, speaking at the company's physical AI conference in Hangzhou on Oct 22, unveiled "Unitree Rehearsal," which he called Unitree's most important project of the year.

The goal is a feedback loop where AI searches research papers, writes robot code, tests it in simulation, and then runs trials on physical robots, with humans still able to judge results and give feedback. Wang said the aim is an automated cycle that could greatly speed up robotics algorithm development. The system is still in development.

Source: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Danish grocer Føtex pilots humanoid robots restocking shelves after hours with HIVE Robots
item.description:
Salling Group's Føtex chain has started training humanoid robots to restock grocery shelves after closing time at a store in Lyngby, north of Copenhagen, through a multi-year partnership with Danish startup HIVE Robots.

  • Unitree builds the hardware; HIVE writes the control software and runs the machine learning, using human "robot pilots" in VR headsets to teach tasks like shelving bags of pasta.
  • Føtex says shelf replenishment takes 40 to 50% of staff time. The robots are still slower than people.
  • HIVE targets commercial deployment by early 2027 on an hourly service fee; Føtex says a full rollout could take up to five years.

Source: ESM Magazine (citing Euronews).

item.title: Tesla starts early Optimus production on Fremont high-volume line; 20,000/week rate at least a year away
item.description:
Tesla's Q3 2026 results on Oct 21 confirmed that Optimus production has started on its high-volume line in Fremont. The shareholder deck says the bots coming off the line are "the first production-quality bots" Tesla has built, and that the manufacturing process has been proven suitable for a commercial product.

  • Musk called it "early production": most of a one-million-unit-per-year line is already installed in Fremont.
  • He expects it will take "at least a year, maybe a little longer" to reach about 20,000 units a week. Parts of the design, reliability, and the robot AI are still being worked on.
  • Deliveries to outside companies are still targeted for around the end of 2027.

Sources: TechCrunch, EV coverage of the earnings call, X story.

item.title: NVIDIA and Agile Robots unveil Agile ONE SN reference humanoid at GTC Berlin; up to 2,000 units in 2027
item.description:
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA expanded its Isaac robotics platform, and Munich's Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack research humanoid preconfigured with Isaac GR00T and powered by Jetson Thor.

  • 1.40 m tall, about 40 kg, 31 degrees of freedom, and dual 20-DoF WUJI Hand 2 hands with tactile sensing.
  • Jetson Thor onboard compute, plus planned integration of the NVIDIA Halos safety stack.
  • Agile's CEO told Reuters that production starts by the end of this year, with 1,000 to 2,000 units planned for next year. Stanford and ETH Zurich are among potential customers.
  • NVIDIA also announced the Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0, and new open data and simulation workflows.

Sources: NVIDIA Newsroom, Reuters via CNA, @NVIDIARobotics on X.

item.title: Unitree reveals H2-X "Kung Fu Legend Guardian" humanoid with about 8-hour endurance
item.description:
Unitree introduced the H2-X "Kung Fu Legend Guardian," a full-size variant of its H2 humanoid. Its launch video shows spinning kicks, flips, a 4-meter drop onto mats, and staged bodyguard and rescue scenes, including lifting a car to free a dummy. The official post passed 3.5 million views within hours.

  • Unitree claims "maximum endurance of approximately 8 hours." Reports say this is standing endurance, compared with about 3 hours for the base H2.
  • Third-party posts list the robot at about 182 cm and 70 kg with 31 DoF. These specs are unconfirmed by Unitree.
  • This is a promotional demo. No price, full spec sheet, or release date has been announced, and the guardian scenes are staged.

Sources: @UnitreeRobotics on X, TechRadar, Humanoids Daily.

item.title: AGCO signs commercial deal to pilot Agility Digit humanoids at Hesston, Kansas factory from 2027
item.description:
Agricultural equipment maker AGCO (Fendt, Massey Ferguson, Valtra) has signed a commercial agreement with Agility Robotics to pilot the Digit humanoid at its Hesston, Kansas, production facility. The pilot is expected to begin in 2027.

  • Initial tasks are parts sorting and stacking, plus placing totes for storage, managed through Agility Arc fleet software.
  • The robot count, contract value, and Digit generation have not been disclosed.
  • The plant makes large, low-volume, highly variable equipment, which Agility pitches as a harder test than an auto line.

Sources: Agility press release, AGCO newsroom, @agilityrobotics on X.

item.title: UC Berkeley SuperMimic trains humanoid whole-body control on one GPU in 3 hours, beating 128-GPU SONIC
item.description:
UC Berkeley researchers (Qiayuan Liao, Kevin Zakka, Pieter Abbeel, Koushil Sreenath and others) released SuperMimic, a humanoid motion tracker that trains through a learned differentiable world model instead of model-free RL. The preprint has been accepted at CoRL 2026.

  • It surpassed the return of the SONIC tracker after 3 hours on one H100. SONIC reported 7 days on 128 L40 GPUs, so this is more than 1,000x fewer GPU-hours.
  • It failed on 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 for SONIC, and reached zero failures after 9.8 hours on two GPUs.
  • The policy ran flips, rolls, and jumps zero-shot on a real Unitree G1.
  • Caveats: the comparison uses different hardware and data sizes, training covered flat ground only, and the real-robot test shows a few motions rather than a measured success rate.

Sources: project page, paper (arXiv 2610.28480), X story.

item.title: Mitsubishi Electric unveils machining system where humanoid robots work with CNC machine tools via physical AI
item.description:
Mitsubishi Electric announced what it calls the industry's first machining system in which general-purpose humanoid robots and CNC machine tools collaborate through physical AI. The humanoids take over operator tasks such as setup, cleaning, removing and transporting finished parts, inspection, and troubleshooting.

  • An AI task planner takes natural-language instructions from operators, generates machining tasks, and splits the work between the CNC machine and the humanoid.
  • The CNC machine exchanges status with the robot in natural language, using Mitsubishi's Maisart AI.
  • A live demo is set for JIMTOF 2026 in Tokyo starting Oct 26.

Source: Mitsubishi Electric press release.

item.title: Samsung tests bipedal humanoid built for 24/7 factory work, eyeing CES 2027 debut (report)
item.description:
Korea JoongAng Daily reports that Samsung Electronics is testing a bipedal humanoid at its Umyeon-dong R&D campus in Seoul. The robot is being trained for repetitive manufacturing and logistics tasks like moving goods, with Samsung and partner staff monitoring it in three shifts to reach around-the-clock operation.

  • The goal is continuous 24/7 work, reportedly helped by swappable batteries.
  • Samsung is reportedly considering a public debut at CES 2027.
  • This is an exclusive media report. Samsung has not formally announced the robot, so treat the details as unconfirmed.

Sources: Korea JoongAng Daily, X post with video.
